quotes.text: A module isn't just a reusable template. That's a technical description. A module is a contract. It says, this is how we do networking in our organization.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Bicep modules as organizational contracts rather than reusable code.

quotes.text: When you write bicep at management groups scope, you're not deploying resources anymore. You're defining the rules that govern how resources can be deployed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why management group scope turns infrastructure code into governance.

quotes.text: Every output you expose is a surface that others will build on. Every output is a contract. When you add an output, you're making a promise.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear design principle for module outputs and hidden coupling.

quotes.text: Drift is the quiet failure mode of infrastructure as code. The template isn't wrong. The infrastructure isn't broken, but they're no longer synchronized.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines configuration drift in a memorable way.

quotes.text: Are you building Azure infrastructure? Is Azure your cloud? Then BICEP is probably the right choice. It's native, it's current, it's simple operationally.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a pragmatic decision rule in the Bicep versus Terraform debate.

takeaways: Enterprise Bicep is about lifecycle, ownership and governance: scope above subscriptions, contracts enforced in parameters and modules, and state managed through deployment stacks.
Management groups, Azure Policy and role assignments defined in Bicep let governance cascade automatically to every subscription and landing zone.
Build on Azure Verified Modules, publish versioned modules to a registry, deploy through gated pipelines and validate continuously against drift.
hook: Most Bicep files are just portal clicks translated into code, which is automation, not architecture. This episode is for Azure architects and platform teams and shows how to use Bicep, deployment stacks, management groups, Azure Policy and Azure Verified Modules to build governed, predictable infrastructure that survives organizational change.
